override.reason: Automated design review is retired/unavailable while being rewritten. Controller-authored DEF, self-reviewed via checklist.verify (one honest partial on f4, no hard-fails); user approved explicitly in chat.

body.title: Review rounds, reconciliation and recovery

summary.prose: This Epic gives every review type -- design review and code review alike -- one shared process for running a review across multiple rounds: a reviewer re-grounds independently each round, a separate reconciliation pass tracks how a correction round relates to the round before it, each round's findings are rendered and presented to the submitter, and a round can recover from a crash without losing already-completed work. It replaces per-review-type checkpoint logic that previously had to be built and recovered separately for each review kind.

body.problem: The review framework has no process for running a review across multiple rounds with reliable recovery. The retired per-review-type implementation duplicated checkpoint/admission logic separately for design review and code review, had no dedicated step for reconciling a new round's findings against a prior round's, had no way to render a round's output for the submitter other than ad hoc chat summaries, and risked the reviewer anchoring on the submitter's own framing of what matters rather than independently re-deriving findings from source. Without a shared process, every review type must separately solve round sequencing, crash recovery, and how a correction round relates to the round before it, and there is no common way to decide, after a correction round runs, whether a previously raised concern has actually been addressed.

nonGoals.text: Reinstating the retired checkpoint model's attempts/chunks/admission/migration-guard machinery
nonGoals.rationale: That machinery is being deliberately replaced by a simpler round-level (or per-Task) checkpoint, not carried forward.

nonGoals.text: Changing the existing ReviewContext data model (round, Scope, ReviewTargets, Comments)
nonGoals.rationale: The data model is already converged and approved under the companion Epic 50cde239426d6e2a; only two specific amendments (header-level reviewId, a corrections array) are fed back to it, not a broader change.

nonGoals.text: Changing the existing 3-round review cap policy itself
nonGoals.rationale: The cap is an existing, separately-decided policy this Epic operates within, not something it revisits.

nonGoals.text: Mid-round resume of in-flight grounding/analysis state
nonGoals.rationale: Round-level checkpointing means recovery is always a full round (or full Task, for code review) restart, never a partial resume of work in progress.

nonGoals.text: Diverging the steering/checklist logic for Correction-and-Re-review from Initial Review beyond what reconciliation already provides
nonGoals.rationale: The two review kinds share one execution process distinguished purely by round number; reconciliation is the only round>1-specific behavior.

nonGoals.text: Letting reconciliation influence the round N gate's block-vs-pass decision
nonGoals.rationale: The gate reads only the current round's own findings; full independent re-grounding already re-catches any defect genuinely still present, and reconciliation is a separate, less reliable judgment that is not a substitute safety net.

nonGoals.text: Mechanically enforcing independent grounding (e.g. stripping or withholding submitter narrative from the reviewer)
nonGoals.rationale: Enforcement is policy/instruction-only via steering; a prior structural claim-extraction mechanism was observed to itself cause tunnel vision by anchoring the reviewer on the submitter's framing.

nonGoals.text: Exposing the docgen render or the checkpoint write as a separate agent-driven step beyond the docgen call itself
nonGoals.rationale: The review-report docgen render is an explicit agent-invoked call, but checkpoint read/write stays internal to the review process, never a step the driving agent must remember to call.

assumptions.text: The companion ReviewContext data-model Epic (50cde239426d6e2a, HLD approved) will incorporate this Epic's two amendments -- a header-level reviewId field and a per-round corrections array -- before this process is implemented against it.

The prior review framework (insrc_review_step/insrc_code_review_step) is fully retired/being rewritten, so this process is not required to preserve backward compatibility with its prior invocation shape or its attempts/chunks/admission/migration-guard checkpoint model.

No generalized round-based checkpoint/temp-folder/reconciliation runtime, and no 'review-report' docgen docType, exist anywhere in the codebase today; the only prior art is per-review-type checkpoint logic that is itself retired.

constraints.text: Checkpoint granularity is defined per review type, not by one universal rule: design review checkpoints at the round level (no natural sub-unit); code review checkpoints per-Task within a round, using Scope's existing tasks: Pointer[] as the natural unit.

Independent grounding is enforced by policy/steering instruction only -- the reviewer is handed the full artifact including submitter narrative and instructed to re-derive independently and disregard it; no technical/structural mechanism strips or withholds that narrative.

The round N approval gate decides block vs. pass from that round's own HIGH/MED findings only; reconciliation (confirmed/still-open/contradicted/no-longer-surfaced) is informational/presentational and never feeds the gate.
Every round performs full independent re-grounding over the entire ReviewTargets scope, ignoring prior findings as input, producing a self-contained finding set.

Reconciliation runs as a separate, dedicated LLM call after a round's findings are finalized (no re-grounding), given the two adjacent rounds' finding sets plus the temp folder's audit trail if needed -- never folded into the same pass that produces the round's findings.

The review-report docgen render is an explicit, agent-invoked docgen docType call (never auto-triggered internally); checkpoint write/read is automatic and internal to the review process (never an agent-driven step).

The .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/ temp folder (per-round input/output, the checkpoint record, rendered MD) is deleted once the review reaches a terminal state, but only after the final round's review-output JSON is copied into the review's durable artifact storage alongside the other persisted artifacts.

The reviewId is one identity, not two: it is both the .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/ folder's own name and a header-level field on ReviewContext, so a resume attempt can recover by reading the id off the artifact/context itself rather than depending solely on caller-side bookkeeping.

stories.title: Initial Review and Correction-and-Re-review share one round-driven execution process
stories.userValue: So that every review, whatever round it is on, runs through one predictable process that always re-derives its own findings from source rather than trusting what came before.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a review starts at round 1 (Initial Review)
acceptanceCriteria.then: it performs full independent re-grounding over the entire ReviewTargets scope, ignoring any prior findings, producing a self-contained finding set

acceptanceCriteria.given: a review is at round > 1 (Correction-and-Re-review) following corrections submitted by the submitter
acceptanceCriteria.then: it executes through the exact same process as round 1, distinguished only by its round number, with no divergent steering or checklist logic beyond reconciliation

acceptanceCriteria.when: the reviewer is handed the full artifact including any submitter rationale
acceptanceCriteria.then: it is instructed via steering to re-derive its findings independently and disregard that narrative, with no structural mechanism stripping or withholding it

localConstraints.text: Initial Review and Correction-and-Re-review share one execution process distinguished purely by round number, with no divergent steering/checklist logic beyond reconciliation.

functionalRequirements.statement: Run every review round, regardless of round number, through the same grounding-and-findings process.
functionalRequirements.rationale: A shared process is what keeps Correction-and-Re-review from silently drifting from Initial Review's behavior.

stories.title: Findings are classified against a fixed taxonomy with a per-review-type-configurable severity scale
stories.userValue: So that findings stay comparable across rounds and review types, while each review type can still set its own severity vocabulary.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a finding is produced in any round
acceptanceCriteria.then: it is classified against exactly one of the fixed taxonomy categories (correctness, functional-completeness, security, quality, maintainability)

acceptanceCriteria.given: a review type's Feedback implementation declares its own severity scale
acceptanceCriteria.when: a finding is recorded for that review type
acceptanceCriteria.then: it carries that configured severity scale, defaulting to HIGH/MED when the review type declares none

localConstraints.text: Every finding is classified against the fixed design-review-specific taxonomy: correctness, functional-completeness, security, quality, maintainability.

The severity scale a finding carries is configured by the controller per review type, defaulting to HIGH/MED, consistent with Feedback being an abstract base type with per-review-type implementations.

functionalRequirements.statement: Classify every finding against the fixed taxonomy and a per-review-type severity scale.
functionalRequirements.rationale: Comparable categorization across rounds and review types is what lets the gate and reconciliation reason about findings uniformly.

stories.title: A dedicated reconciliation pass tracks prior findings without ever gating approval
stories.userValue: So that the submitter and reviewer can see how a correction round's independent findings relate to what was raised before, without that judgment ever deciding approval itself.

acceptanceCriteria.then: it executes as a separate LLM call reading only the two adjacent rounds' finding sets, plus the temp folder's audit trail if needed, with no re-grounding

acceptanceCriteria.given: reconciliation has classified a prior round's HIGH/MED finding as confirmed, still-open, contradicted, or no-longer-surfaced
acceptanceCriteria.when: round N's approval gate evaluates block vs. pass
acceptanceCriteria.then: the gate decision uses only round N's own HIGH/MED findings and is unaffected by the reconciliation classification

functionalRequirements.statement: Run a reconciliation pass after each round's findings are finalized, classifying each of the prior round's HIGH/MED findings as confirmed, still-open, contradicted, or no-longer-surfaced.
functionalRequirements.rationale: Reconciliation gives visibility into round-over-round disposition without becoming a second, less reliable gate.

stories.title: Each round's findings are rendered and presented through a new review-report docgen document
stories.userValue: So that the submitter can see and act on each round's outcome through a persisted, reviewable document rather than an ephemeral chat summary.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a round's findings, and for round > 1 its reconciliation, have finished
acceptanceCriteria.when: the agent explicitly invokes the review-report docgen docType with the review id and round
acceptanceCriteria.then: it renders a persisted MD artifact for that round

acceptanceCriteria.given: a correction round's MD is rendered and the submitter's corrections entries addressed or rejected specific prior Feedback this round
acceptanceCriteria.then: it annotates only those specifically addressed or rejected prior Feedback items as resolved/still-open/contradicted, not a running audit of all prior history

acceptanceCriteria.given: a round's review-report MD has been rendered
acceptanceCriteria.then: it is presented to the user via insrc_present every round, with no response required from the user until the existing 3-round cap is reached

localConstraints.text: A round's review-report MD shows only that round's own findings, with inline resolved/still-open/contradicted annotations limited to whichever prior Feedback the submitter's corrections entries actually addressed or rejected this round -- never a running audit of all history.

functionalRequirements.statement: Render each round's outcome to a persisted MD artifact via a new public docgen docType and present it to the user every round.
functionalRequirements.rationale: A persisted, explicitly-invoked document is what makes each round's outcome auditable and reviewable after the fact.

stories.title: Per-review-type checkpointing and temp-folder lifecycle make a review resumable and its final result durable
stories.userValue: So that a crash costs at most one unit of rework, and a completed review's result survives after its scratch working folder is gone.

acceptanceCriteria.when: a round's full cycle (grounding, findings, reconciliation, MD render, present) completes
acceptanceCriteria.then: the review process automatically writes a checkpoint at the granularity defined for its review type -- round-level for design review, per-Task for code review -- with no agent-driven step

acceptanceCriteria.given: a crash occurs before a round's full cycle completes
acceptanceCriteria.then: only the in-flight unit of work (the round, or the in-flight Task for code review) is re-run, not units already completed

acceptanceCriteria.given: a review reaches a terminal state
acceptanceCriteria.when: its .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/ temp folder is due to be deleted
acceptanceCriteria.then: the final round's review-output JSON is first copied into the review's durable artifact storage before deletion occurs

acceptanceCriteria.given: a review is resumed after an interruption
acceptanceCriteria.when: the resuming call supplies the reviewId
acceptanceCriteria.then: the system locates the review's prior state, because reviewId is the same identity as both ReviewContext's header-level field and the temp folder's name

localConstraints.text: A review's checkpoint is a generic 'review checkpoint' JSON side-record, independent of ReviewContext's own fields, stored inside the .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/ folder.

functionalRequirements.statement: Checkpoint a review at the granularity appropriate to its review type, written/read automatically and invisibly, and copy the final round's output into durable storage before the temp folder is deleted.
functionalRequirements.rationale: Minimal, per-type-appropriate recovery and durable final results are what makes the process trustworthy across crashes.

requirements.statement: Run Initial Review and Correction-and-Re-review as one shared execution process, distinguished purely by round number (round 1 vs round > 1), with no divergent steering/checklist logic beyond reconciliation.
requirements.rationale: A single process keeps the two review kinds from drifting apart in behavior that reconciliation does not already account for.

requirements.statement: Perform full independent re-grounding over the entire ReviewTargets scope every round, ignoring prior findings as input, so every round produces a self-contained finding set.
requirements.rationale: Independent re-grounding is what lets a correction round genuinely re-catch a defect that is still present, rather than trusting a prior round's or the submitter's account of it.

requirements.statement: Classify every finding against a fixed design-review-specific taxonomy (correctness, functional-completeness, security, quality, maintainability) with a severity scale that is controller-configured per review type, defaulting to HIGH/MED.
requirements.rationale: A fixed taxonomy keeps findings comparable across rounds and review types while leaving room for a different review type's Feedback implementation to configure its own severity scale.

requirements.statement: Run a dedicated reconciliation pass after each round's findings are finalized, classifying each of the prior round's HIGH/MED findings as confirmed, still-open, contradicted, or no-longer-surfaced.
requirements.rationale: Reconciliation is what tells the submitter and reviewer how a correction round's independent findings relate to what was raised before, without that judgment ever gating approval itself.

requirements.statement: Render each round's findings (plus, for round > 1, the reconciliation annotations relevant to that round's own corrections) to a persisted MD artifact via a new public docgen docType, and present it to the user every round.
requirements.rationale: A persisted, presentable artifact per round is what lets the submitter see and act on each round's outcome, and keeps the review's record auditable after the fact.

requirements.statement: Maintain a checkpoint record, written and read automatically and invisibly by the review process, at the granularity appropriate to the review type (round-level for design review, per-Task for code review), so a crash re-runs only the in-flight unit of work.
requirements.rationale: Per-review-type granularity keeps recovery minimal without forcing one review type's unit of work onto another that does not share its structure.

requirements.statement: Copy the final round's review-output JSON into the review's durable artifact storage before deleting the .insrc/tmp/<reviewId>/ temp folder at a terminal state.
requirements.rationale: The completed result must stay recoverable and referenceable after the ephemeral working folder is gone, even though the intermediate round material does not need to persist.

requirements.statement: Run every review round, regardless of round number, through the same grounding-and-findings process.
requirements.rationale: A shared process is what keeps Correction-and-Re-review from silently drifting from Initial Review's behavior.

requirements.statement: Classify every finding against the fixed taxonomy and a per-review-type severity scale.
requirements.rationale: Comparable categorization across rounds and review types is what lets the gate and reconciliation reason about findings uniformly.

requirements.statement: Run a reconciliation pass after each round's findings are finalized, classifying each of the prior round's HIGH/MED findings as confirmed, still-open, contradicted, or no-longer-surfaced.
requirements.rationale: Reconciliation gives visibility into round-over-round disposition without becoming a second, less reliable gate.

requirements.statement: Render each round's outcome to a persisted MD artifact via a new public docgen docType and present it to the user every round.
requirements.rationale: A persisted, explicitly-invoked document is what makes each round's outcome auditable and reviewable after the fact.

requirements.statement: Checkpoint a review at the granularity appropriate to its review type, written/read automatically and invisibly, and copy the final round's output into durable storage before the temp folder is deleted.
requirements.rationale: Minimal, per-type-appropriate recovery and durable final results are what makes the process trustworthy across crashes.
